hypothesis: On a HIP card below 10 GiB of --vram the dense mirrors, and the shared experts with them, stay in RAM, so the prompt's VRAM bank (COLI_CUDA_MOE_BATCH=1) can never run; treating it as not asked for frees the bank-sized VRAM reserve for decode mirrors and keeps the prefill pool on, which cuts the prompt's expert reads several times and shortens the time to the first token.
model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash architecture, REAP-pruned to 132 experts x 43 layers (79 GB), safetensors, native FP8/FP4
command: make -C c -j16 deepseek-v4 HIP=1 HIP_ARCH=gfx1102 ROCM_HOME=/usr on dev (baseline) and on this commit (trial); deepseek_v4 <model> --prompt-file long_prompt.txt --max-tokens 12 with the environment in config; the arms alternate (trial, baseline) four times; tok_s = 2535 prompt tokens / time_to_first_token from the engine's `timing` line (prompt throughput); memory: the engine's automatic RAM budget (55 to 58 GiB available at start, 42 to 45 GiB expert cache in every run)

hardware.storage: Apacer AS2280Q4U 4TB NVMe, ext4 (rw,noatime), direct aligned reads
hardware.os: Gentoo Linux 7.3.1, gcc 16.2.1, ROCm/HIP 7.16.0 (clang 23.1.5), AMD Radeon RX 7600M XT 8 GB (gfx1102; also the display GPU, desktop and other software running, load average 13 to 19 during the later runs)

quality.method: greedy text identical across the arm's runs and identical to the trial's (md5 of stdout)
